To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
artificial aptazymes can knockdown expression from viral genes, and that this can be used for the study of viral gene function or as a safety mechanism in oncolytic virus-based cancer therapies.
artificial riboswitch technology, i.e. small molecule–inducible self-cleaving RNA enzymes, enables control of biological outcomes of DNA and RNA virus infections.

we have developed artificial aptazymes for gene expression regulation of DNA and, importantly, RNA viruses, and that they function independently of transcriptional machinery, making them a promising alternative to inducible promoters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of artificial riboswitch-based control of gene expression in eukaryotes.
the development of new tools for basic research and applications in medicine.
the development and application of artificial RNA switches for control of viral gene expression and replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aptazymes are small and ligand-dependent riboswitches that are able to control gene expression and biological outcomes in e.g. DNA and RNA viruses, thus representing universally applicable tools for gene regulation in eukaryotes.
the use of artificial riboswitch technology in viruses is a new approach to control gene expression and biological outcomes in eucaryotic systems.

this study provides the first evidence of artificial riboswitch function in fully cytoplasimic (viral) genetic systems, demonstrating the potential of aptazymes for applications in gene expression control of viruses and eukaryotic cells in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
artificial riboswitch technology has the potential to revolutionize the field of gene expression regulation in eukaryotes, and that it can be applied to a broad range of viral and cellular systems.
artificial riboswitch technology is a promising tool for gene regulation in eukaryotes, and that it is now established for application in DNA- and RNA viruses, including human pathogens.

we have developed an artificial riboswtich for gene expression control that is small and RNA-intrinsic, and can be triggered by various small molecules, which is applicable in fully cytoplamic systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
artificial riboswitch-based regulation of gene expression in eukaryotes is possible and may represent a valuable tool for future studies.
artificial riboswitch technology can be applied to control replication of human-pathogenic RNA and DNA viruses.
the artificial riboswitch technology, which is based on the aptazyme principle, is generally applicable for control of DNA and/or RNA virus gene expression.
